question: Which mechanism correctly distinguishes benzodiazepines from barbiturates at the GABA-A receptor?

answers.text: Benzodiazepines increase the frequency of Cl⁻ channel opening; barbiturates increase the duration — and can open the channel directly without GABA at high doses

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. BZDs require GABA to be present (allosteric modulation only) and increase how often the channel opens — this ceiling effect explains their wider therapeutic index. Barbiturates increase how long each opening lasts and at supra-therapeutic doses bypass GABA entirely, explaining their dose-dependent respiratory depression.

answers.text: Benzodiazepines increase the duration of Cl⁻ channel opening; barbiturates increase the frequency

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is the reverse of the correct answer. A useful mnemonic: Ben(zodiazepines) = Frequency; Bar(biturates) = duRation. BZDs bind at the α-γ interface; barbiturates bind at the β-subunit.

answers.text: Both agents act identically on GABA-A — only their pharmacokinetic half-lives differ

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Their mechanisms are fundamentally different. This difference has critical clinical implications: barbiturates can cause fatal respiratory depression without a ceiling (direct channel opening), while BZDs have a ceiling effect and a specific reversal agent (flumazenil).

answers.text: Benzodiazepines block GABA-A while barbiturates activate it — they have opposite mechanisms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both BZDs and barbiturates are GABA-A potentiators (positive allosteric modulators) — they enhance GABAergic inhibition. Neither blocks the receptor. Their distinction lies in how they modulate channel kinetics.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: BZDs = frequency increase (require GABA = ceiling effect = safer); barbiturates = duration increase (can open without GABA = no ceiling = narrow therapeutic index). This distinction determines clinical safety profiles.

This mechanistic difference (frequency vs duration; ceiling vs no ceiling) is the pharmacological basis for the safety advantage of BZDs over barbiturates and explains why flumazenil reverses BZDs but no reversal agent exists for barbiturates.
